controls.controlName: Hermetic jobs and workflow execution controls
controls.proofBoundary: Hermetic proof covers classification, tenant context, service actor execution, PDP checks, bounded retry, idempotency, dead-letter evidence, redaction, schedules, approvals, audit, and local read/list controls.

controls.controlName: Workflow provider, scheduler, queue, replay, and high-risk automation depth
controls.riskStatement: Jobs/workflows can only be treated as local control evidence until durable live workflow, queue, scheduler, replay, backup, and automation-provider behaviour is implemented and proven.
controls.threatFailureScenario: A false closure would allow Temporal, Windmill, queue, cron, replay, or high-risk automation controls to be treated as production-capable without proving retry, drain, pause/resume, backpressure, migration, or recovery behaviour.
controls.affectedAssetService: jobs-workflows; workflow-engine-temporal-composed-test; workflow-engine-windmill-composed-test; event-bus; scheduler; operational automation
controls.treatment: defer-with-owner; keep source issue open; require future proof for live workflow provider, queue/worker cluster, replay/migration, transactional outbox/inbox, quotas/backpressure, drain, backup/restore, dry-run gates, cron schedules, heartbeats, egress, and observability before stronger claims.
controls.proofBoundary: Existing proof is hermetic-local only and does not prove live Temporal, Windmill, queue, worker cluster, production cron, or provider recovery.

domainRows.linearParentKnown: USF-152; related to USF-133; do not reparent without coordinator approval

controls.controlName: Hermetic notification template, consent, provider config, job, retry, and audit controls
controls.proofBoundary: Hermetic proof covers tenant scope, template approval, recipient/address redaction, consent suppression, SecretReference provider config, idempotent delivery jobs, bounded retry/dead-letter evidence, and audit.

controls.controlName: Notification persistence, transactional outbox, feedback, unsubscribe, provider, deliverability, campaign, retention, and circuit-breaker depth
controls.riskStatement: Notification controls cannot be treated as complete until persistence, outbox, provider feedback, unsubscribe ingestion, live delivery, deliverability, bulk/campaign, retention purge, verification, and circuit breakers are proven.
controls.threatFailureScenario: A false closure would allow lost notifications, suppressed unsubscribe/bounce handling, unbounded campaign delivery, or provider failure to be missed while appearing Done.
controls.affectedAssetService: notifications; notification providers; notification logs; delivery jobs; recipient addresses
controls.treatment: defer-with-owner; preserve USF-153 as follow-up; do not reparent; require future DB-backed persistence, transactional outbox, bounce/complaint ingestion, unsubscribe routes, live providers, deliverability, campaign runtime, rate limits, retention purge, address verification, provider circuit breakers, and API/UI proof.
controls.proofBoundary: Existing proof is hermetic-local only and does not prove production SMTP, SMS, push, webhook providers, deliverability, legal certification, or live-provider posture.

controls.controlName: Hermetic API contract, OpenAPI, guard, envelope, idempotency, and pagination controls
controls.proofBoundary: Hermetic proof covers route contract mapping, OpenAPI safety, missing-tenant and tenant-mismatch denial, PDP denial, side-effecting idempotency, safe errors, and pagination cursor safety.

controls.controlName: GraphQL, federation, generated clients, public compatibility, browser CSRF/cookie runtime, advanced queries, quotas, gateway, TLS/WAF, and deprecation depth
controls.riskStatement: The API surface cannot claim public or compatibility readiness until gateway, browser-session, GraphQL/federation, client generation, schema drift, abuse quota, TLS/WAF, and deprecation controls are implemented and proven.
controls.threatFailureScenario: A false closure would expose unproven compatibility or gateway controls, allowing unsafe client contracts, CSRF/cookie assumptions, or unsupported public API stability claims.
controls.affectedAssetService: API contracts; OpenAPI; browser sessions; gateway/proxy; developer clients
controls.treatment: defer-with-owner; retain USF-155 and link future gateway/operator work to USF-180 where applicable; require future proof for GraphQL/federation, generated clients, compatibility, CSRF/cookie runtime, advanced query semantics, quota/abuse controls, bulk APIs, gateway/trusted proxy, TLS/WAF, and deprecation.
controls.proofBoundary: Existing proof is hermetic Fastify/OpenAPI control evidence and does not prove public API, external SDK, production gateway, TLS/WAF, or browser-session readiness.

controls.controlName: Hermetic provider registry, mode, SecretReference, redaction, fail-closed, and import-boundary controls
controls.proofBoundary: Hermetic proof covers explicit provider modes, categories, owners, SecretReference-only credentials, redacted status, disabled/deferred/unavailable fail-closed behaviour, audit metadata, and adapter-boundary SDK imports.

controls.controlName: Live provider authority, supplier, egress, TLS, circuit breaker, drift, incident, failover, cache/search/gateway/observability, and readiness aggregation depth
controls.riskStatement: Provider readiness remains bounded until live-external-authorised authority, supplier/subprocessor governance, egress, TLS/certs, circuit breakers, drift detection, incident hooks, failover, and composed readiness aggregation are proven.
controls.threatFailureScenario: A false closure would let composed provider availability or local registry entries masquerade as live-provider authorisation, supplier approval, or production resilience.
controls.affectedAssetService: provider registry; provider adapters; external provider candidates; cache/search/gateway/observability provider dependencies
controls.treatment: defer-with-owner; retain USF-157; require future proof for composed-provider scope reconciliation, live-external-authorised mode, supplier/subprocessor workflow, egress allow-listing, TLS/certs, circuit breakers/timeouts/fallback/bulkheads, drift detection, incident hooks, failover/DR, cache/search/gateway/observability provider depth, and composed readiness aggregation.
controls.proofBoundary: Existing proof is local/dev/test control evidence and does not prove live external providers, supplier approval, SOC, ISO, production, or regulatory certification.

controls.controlName: Hermetic rate-limit, quota, backpressure, safe denial, audit, and telemetry controls
controls.proofBoundary: Hermetic proof covers fixed-window rate limits, tenant-isolated quotas, fail-closed policy validation, idempotent accounting, safe denial evidence, audit, and telemetry signals.

controls.controlName: Distributed enforcement, gateway/edge/WAF/CDN/bot/fraud, rollout, operator API, policy approval, cost quota, IP privacy, and abuse operations depth
controls.riskStatement: Guardrails remain local/dev/test evidence until distributed counters, multi-node consistency, live gateway/edge enforcement, WAF/CDN/bot/fraud controls, and abuse operations are proven.
controls.threatFailureScenario: A false closure would let single-node guardrails be treated as distributed abuse protection, causing fail-open rate limits, quota bypass, or ungoverned policy rollout.
controls.affectedAssetService: guardrails; API gateway; edge/WAF/CDN; abuse controls; telemetry and audit records
controls.treatment: defer-with-owner; retain USF-161; require future proof for distributed counters, multi-node consistency, live edge/gateway enforcement, WAF/CDN/bot/fraud provider posture, route rollout, operator guardrail APIs, policy approval workflow, cost quotas, IP privacy, and production abuse operations.
controls.proofBoundary: Existing proof is single-node in-memory local/dev/test control evidence and does not prove live WAF, edge, gateway, bot, fraud, abuse-provider, SOC, ISO, or production readiness.

controls.controlName: Hermetic bulk metadata, PDP, guardrail, quarantine, job, audit, telemetry, preview, and evidence manifest controls
controls.proofBoundary: Hermetic proof covers tenant-scoped bulk metadata, PDP, guardrails, file quarantine, jobs, audit, telemetry, deterministic preview, format safety, and evidence-package manifest hashes.

controls.controlName: HTTP/OpenAPI surfaces, migration runtime, resumable applier, live transfer providers, parser adapters, decompression controls, rollback, approval, purge, legal hold, eDiscovery, regulatory, and production migration depth
controls.riskStatement: Import/export/bulk remains local/dev/test evidence until deep runtime, live transfer, resumable mutation, rollback, legal hold, eDiscovery, retention, and regulatory export behaviour is implemented and proven.
controls.threatFailureScenario: A false closure would allow destructive import/export or regulatory data movement to proceed without proof for rollback, compensation, approval separation, purge, retention, decompression-bomb controls, or legal hold constraints.
controls.affectedAssetService: import-export-bulk; file storage; jobs; guardrails; audit evidence; tenant data exports and imports
controls.treatment: defer-with-owner; retain USF-163; require future proof for broad HTTP/OpenAPI surfaces, production migration runtime, transactional resumable import applier, live transfer providers, parser adapters, decompression-bomb controls, rollback/compensation workflows, approval/SoD depth, export purge/retention scheduler, legal hold workflow runtime, legal/eDiscovery/regulatory export evidence, and production migration evidence if ever authorised.
controls.proofBoundary: Existing proof is hermetic local/dev/test governed data-movement evidence and does not prove production, legal, regulatory, eDiscovery, live-provider, or production migration readiness.
